precepts.label: Psalms 17:15
precepts.why:
Men, we want dominion. We want rulership; we want to subdue the nations. God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion,” and he told them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.” Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything under foot.

When you read “after our likeness,” understand it is more than what you look like. At that time everybody was of color, yet God gave a specific people rulership. David shows what the likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is not just appearance; it is being righteous. Christ is black, God is black, and we are made after his image, but the image alone does not bring the dominion. In being righteous we will subdue and have dominion over things.

So the government must be in place, and in that we must be keeping the commandments. It is the only way we are going to get it. That government cannot happen unless we are righteous.

precepts.label: Zechariah 2:6-7
precepts.why:
Jacob called his sons to tell them “that which shall befall you in the last days,” and of Judah he said, “thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies.” That says two things: Judah will be fighting his enemy, and Judah will be living in close proximity to his enemy, who today is Esau, Edom. Zechariah 2 is the scripture that proves Judah will be living with that enemy.

“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.” Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Zion is the city of Judah. The daughter of Babylon, as Psalms 137 shows, is Edom, the Caucasian race. So Zion is dwelling with the daughter of Babylon: Judah living in the land of the north, in the house of his enemy.

That is the picture of Genesis 49:8. Judah’s hand in the neck of his enemies is Judah living with him and contending with him. In the 1960s and 70s there was the Black Panthers, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X, and many movements where Judah rose up and fought the so-called white man. “he stooped down, he couched as a lion,” and at one point it looked like he was about to strike.

But the lion lay back down: “as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?” Christ is the one who will rouse him up. Until then the word to Zion is to come forth and deliver himself from the daughter of Babylon he dwells with.

precepts.label: Exodus 1:16-17
precepts.why:
Pharaoh’s crafty counsel had a plan behind it, and here it is: “When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.”

What they were hoping for was to run into Hebrew women who hated themselves and hated their people, so their plan could be executed. They were doing it by proxy of the midwives, hoping the midwives felt the way the rebellious Israelites felt coming out of Egypt: we miss the garlics, we miss the leeks, take us back, we like being a slave. They were hoping they loved their enemy and hated themselves.

“But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.” That means the midwives loved their people. They feared God, and the way they showed it was that they loved their people.

The enemies of Israel have always capitalized off of our hatred of ourselves. What was commanded in Egypt is what abortion has evolved into: make the babies that come out of Israelite wombs vanish. Now the black mind has been so twisted and perverted that they do not even have to put out an edict that says kill the children. The black woman will do it herself, and she is already doing it by the millions. That is a genocide in itself.

That is why we must be the ones to correct this, to highlight it, illuminate it, and set the nation back in order: restore the love of ourselves and the fear of God, and show that the enemy hates us.

precepts.label: Luke 1:68-74
precepts.why:
Leviticus 26 says that even “when they be in the land of their enemies”, like today here in America, “I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”. Then: “But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”. Who said bloodline ain’t important? The Bible says he will remember the covenant of your ancestors. Luke 1 is saying the same thing in the New Testament.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of salvation is Christ. He is the king, out of the house of David. “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. That is what Leviticus 26 is saying: in the land of their enemies he will not cast them away.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers”, our ancestors, “and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”. That is the covenant of the ancestors in Leviticus 26:45, remembered for their sakes and brought to pass through Christ.

And what is it for? “that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. The God who brought our fathers out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen has not broken his covenant with us. He will deliver us out of the hand of our enemies so that we serve him without fear.

precepts.label: James 2:1
precepts.why:
Moses charged the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. You shall not have respect of persons in judgment; you cannot be partial. You have to hear both sides, the small as well as the great. That is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position.

James speaks of the same thing: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Here is respect of persons, and James sets it against the faith of Christ itself. You cannot hold the faith of the Lord of glory and at the same time judge one brother by a different measure than another.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man”. You are not here to be loved or to be liked; you are judges. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them, and some get offended when judgment falls on their friend, even without knowing what happened. What does that have to do with you? The judgment is God's, and a judge in Israel must be just, not partial.

precepts.label: James 2:4
precepts.why:
“Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” Respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another: respecting one over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother or those brothers. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration for advantage; there is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

And here is the end result: you “are become judges of evil thoughts”. Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them. Whether he gives you gifts, whether he is your ride to Sabbath, whether he got you a job, whatever the case may be, now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord says that is an evil, evil thing.

So you might think, I am just not going to judge because that is my friend. The Bible says you are evil. That is exactly what Moses forbade when he charged the judges to “judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

precepts.label: James 2:9
precepts.why:
“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But if you have respect of persons, whether in judgment or in having men's persons in admiration for advantage, you commit sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God.

You want to be in that position, but much is required of you in the position as judges. You must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy: judge righteous judgment, whether it is your friend or not. In a position of leadership you cannot conceal your friend's folly; none of us should.

What has been discovered is that because someone is your friend, you do not want to speak out. You do not want to reveal the sin, as Leviticus 5:1 requires, and you do not want to be part of the judgment once the sin is revealed. You sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you do not agree with the judgment God says to bring forth. Something is wrong with that. We have to stand on what God said. Anyone you consider a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give us a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:26
precepts.why:
“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” Why a sign? When you see a McDonald's sign, it lets you know a McDonald's is there. The curses have to be upon us for a sign because we would be cut off from our heritage, and in the future Judah will need to identify who Israel is. How do you identify the Israelites today? By the curses.

Deuteronomy 32:26 shows why: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. We were scattered into corners in slavery, and the remembrance of who we are, our nationality, all of it, has ceased from among men. We did not just forget because time went on. We forgot because the nations made war with us and took crafty counsel: make sure those slaves cannot read and write. They destroyed us as a people and took our nationality. Ask a Chinese man today who the Israelites are, and he points at the fake people in the land, the synagogue of Satan.

Yet go to Africa today and you will see millions of people professing that they are the people of God, the Israelites, though you will not see it on the news. Just in Nigeria there is a large Israelite community of millions. Over generations of misinterpretation and mixing customs with the Hamitic tribes they do not keep the laws the way they are supposed to, but they always knew they were Israel.

So God did it real nice. Esau would take our nationality from us, but the curses would follow us and our seed, so that no matter where we are scattered, in Africa, America, South America, China, Iran, the islands, when we read the Bible we say: wait, this is talking about my people.

precepts.label: Zechariah 12:7
precepts.why:
“Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people”. There is Judah in Africa too, but this is speaking of Judah on this side of the earth, in the Western Hemisphere, specifically in the United States of America. Judah in North America is under Esau, who controls the world right now, and with an American passport you can go anywhere in the world. A Jamaican, Haitian or Nigerian passport cannot take you everywhere. That is why we tell you brothers: get your passport.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”. God is going to raise up the tribe of Judah first, Judah in America. Then, when it says bring him unto his people, it means Judah will know where God's people are and will go find them. Wherever our people are in Africa, in Japan, in Iran, in India, scattered throughout the four corners of the earth, Judah will be able to identify them, find them, and teach them what God commanded of them.

That is why Genesis 49 speaks mainly of Israel on this side of the world: Judah needed to know who they were first. And it is already happening. The bishops and brothers that travel went into the history of the people, and they found Judah among the Igbo of Nigeria and the tribes scattered across Africa, India and the islands, now written on the revised twelve tribe chart. When people ask how we know, it is because the Lord showed us; the spirit guided us. That is “be thou an help to him from his enemies”: God is a help to Judah, making us find things so we are not guessing, and the chart will keep being updated as the Lord reveals more.

classes.title: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:7
precepts.why:
Assyria had already taken the northern kingdom around 722 BC, and around 701 they came for Judah. Their ambassador was talking big: we are going to wipe the floor with you, destroy you and bring you into slavery. Then came a letter of threats. And look at what Hezekiah did with it: he “went up into the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord.” He took the letter, spread it out before him, and began to pray: “thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth”.

That is what Peter teaches: “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” Sometimes we get in situations and fear comes upon us. Go before the Lord. Whatever the problem is, the Lord knows; go before him and spread it out before him, the way Hezekiah did.

And the Lord answered. Isaiah was not in the room when Hezekiah prayed, but the Lord told him to go to the king and say, “That which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.” That is how you know Isaiah was a prophet. Hezekiah cast his care upon the Lord, and that same night one angel smote 185,000 Assyrians.

precepts.label: Matthew 12:36
precepts.why:
The Lord asks Sennacherib, “Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Israel.” By his messengers he had reproached the Lord with his boasting words, and every one of them came up into the Lord's ears: “thy rage against me and thy tumult is come up into mine ears”. The same words also remind our people how we have despised the Lord.

Christ said, “every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.” We have to be mindful of this. Sometimes we speak frivolous things and don't realize the Most High is recording everything. Idle means idolatrous: every idolatrous word we speak.

Sennacherib's words were recorded and answered: the Lord put his hook in his nose and turned him back the way he came. So be careful what comes out of your mouth; the Most High hears it all and will bring it to account.

precepts.label: Job 11:6
precepts.why:
When you go to the Christian commentaries on Isaiah 33, many of them refer it back to this history: Hezekiah, the king of Assyria, and the angel that wiped them all out. They try to keep every prophecy in the past, as history that already happened. That is why the apologists love to say, that happened already: they read a Christian commentary that said so.

But the scriptures have dual meanings. Job says he “would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” We all want to know the secrets of wisdom, and they are double to that which is written. You read something, but it has a double meaning behind it. That's how the scriptures are written.

So Isaiah 33:1, “Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee!”, was Assyria; but guess who also does that today? The United States of America. To spoil means to rob: the oil of Venezuela, the riches of Libya and of Saddam Hussein, Iran, which did nothing to America. “when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled”. The history of 2 Kings 19 happened, and the same word speaks to our day.

precepts.label: Hosea 5:15
precepts.why:
“He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.” When our people are oppressed, God opens their ears. All the things Trump is doing, and ICE is doing in the streets and in the black community, are God opening your ears. For the last 60 years our people have been lost and confused, following the American dream and thinking America is about equal rights and opportunity. God said, no, this place is not your rest. So he turns up the oppression, because that is the only time we as a people turn to God: when bad things start happening to us.

Hosea says it: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” Until we acknowledge our offence and seek God's face.

In our affliction we will seek him early: before it is too late, before we die, before judgment comes. So God is allowing Trump to do these things in the black community with these ICE agents so that you will seek him. Our people are realizing that the American dream is exactly what it is, a dream, and that there is no such thing here as justice and equal rights. That is why judgment starts first with the house of God.

precepts.label: Psalms 78:33
precepts.why:
Psalm 78 shows the same pattern: “Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, and their years in trouble.” The trouble is affliction. “When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned and enquired early after God.”

When God slew us. What do you see taking place all over the streets right now? Our people being oppressed, locked up, put in prison by ICE officers. Then we seek God. That is when we return and enquire early after the Lord: when bad things start happening to us.

That is why judgment must begin first at the house of the Lord. Number one, for us to turn back to our God. Number two, to prove us: as you turn to him, bad things will happen to see whether you believe and trust in him. “And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their redeemer.” He is the one who will redeem us from the condition we are in.

And Isaiah 30 gives the teachers their job: though the Lord gives the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, the teachers will not be removed into a corner any more. As our people cry under the affliction, we go to them and tell them why it is happening: this is the way, walk ye in it. Not guns, as some are calling for; the word of God is what will change our people and bring destruction on this place.

precepts.label: Proverbs 10:18
precepts.why:
“Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off”: God will cut you off, cut off from the book of the living. Proverbs shows what is really behind slander: “He that hideth hatred with lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, is a fool.”

When somebody lies on you or slanders you, what that really says is that there is hatred there. The lying lips are hiding hatred.

“and he that uttereth a slander”: you had Tyre Gas, you had Lightfoot, you had these guys uttering slanders, and their followers talk that way because their leaders are the same way. They run with slander. As a leader you are supposed to hear an outrageous lie and say, I do not believe that. One woman said we came to Canada on a magic school bus, and some leaders believed it.

God says you are a fool to listen to lies, run with them and put them out there. Slander is defamation: running with an accusation without two or three witnesses, and God cuts that man off.

precepts.label: Proverbs 26:28
precepts.why:
“A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.” If you lie on somebody and run with slander, it says that you hate the one who is afflicted by it.

You heard it plainly from one of them: I am here to down IUIC. That is the hatred behind the lying tongue that Psalms 101 says God will cut off.

Every matter is to be established by two or three witnesses. What was put out about Captain Obadiah was one witness, and that witness was a lie. The charges were dropped; the footage and the witnesses showed he was defending himself. It is sad that the white man had to come and say he was defending himself, when those who talk about righteous judgment could not understand something that simple. In London, when our sister died, people said IUIC killed her and hid evidence, and the investigators showed that the man who did it was evil and we had nothing to do with it.

A false witness is called slander, or defamation, and false witness can get you killed. By the law, what was to be done to the brother you slandered is to be done unto you. We do not have power to institute that, but Esau’s court system has defamation, and that is how it is going to be done now: whatever you put out against the truth, you had better be able to prove it, or you will have to come up out of the pockets. That is to protect the ministry of Christ, because the lies are put out to blame the ministry.

precepts.label: Sirach 11:9
precepts.why:
“Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.” That is why so many brothers get caught up in suits: striving in things that do not concern them, things they know nothing about. You just hear something and you are running your mouth.

To sit in judgment with sinners is sitting in counsel with brothers that are not right, brothers who were put out of the school, like Judah Mack and Titus.

Read on: “My son, meddle not with many matters: for if thou meddle much, thou shalt not be innocent.” This is for those who keep running their mouths talking about us. You meddle in matters that do not concern you, and you are not going to be innocent. That is why legal measures are being taken: to teach men to control their mouths, and to make sure that when you say something, it is true.

So the privy slanderer of Psalms 101 is the man who strives in what does not concern him and sits with sinners, and God will cut him off.

thread.text: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.

classes.title: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 11:18
precepts.why:
The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people, Israel. So what did Solomon mean, in his righteousness, when he said “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”? The heart is the mind. What is set as a seal upon our mind and upon our arm? Is it the six-point hexagram? Heck no. Here is what he was referring to.

“Therefore shall ye lay up these my words in your heart and in your soul”. These my words are the laws of God, laid up in your heart, meaning your mind. “and bind them for a sign upon your hand, that they may be as frontlets between your eyes.” In ancient times Israel would write the laws on leather and wrap them around their arms. Those were the frontlets, and the frontlets between your eyes are on your forehead.

So go back to the Song: “Set me as a seal upon thine heart”, that's the mind; “as a seal upon thine arm”. The seal is the law, the laws of God, the words of God, bound on the arm and laid up in the mind. People who will not be proven wrong search for scriptures that use the word shield or seal and try to make them say it is the Star of David, forcing a square peg into a circle. That is a complete lie; the seal is the law.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 10:21-23
precepts.why:
Ezra lays out everything Israel lost: “our sanctuary is laid waste, our altar broken down, our temple destroyed; Our psaltery is laid on the ground”. The psaltery is the music. “our song is put to silence, our rejoicing is at an end, the light of our candlestick is put out”, the menorah is put out. “the ark of our covenant is spoiled, our holy things are defiled, and the name that is called upon us is almost profaned”, the name Israel.

It goes on: “our children are put to shame, our priests are burnt, our Levites are gone into captivity, our virgins are defiled, and our wives ravished”, our wives were raped; “our righteous men carried away, our little ones destroyed, our young men are brought in bondage, and our strong men are become weak”.

Then: “And, which is the greatest of all, the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour; for she is delivered into the hands of them that hate us.” What is the seal of Zion? Is that talking about the six-point hexagram, the star of Remphan, the star of Moloch? No. Isaiah shows what the seal of Zion is: the law.

So the seal Solomon asked to be set upon the heart and the arm is the same seal of Zion Ezra mourned: the law of God. The greatest of all Israel's losses was not a symbol but the honour of the law, delivered into the hands of them that hate us.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
Ezra said “the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour”. Here is what the seal of Zion is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” Seal the law among my disciples. The law is the seal. The law is the seal.

That is what Solomon meant by “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”: the law of God set on the mind and bound on the arm, as Deuteronomy said to bind the words for a sign upon the hand. It is not the six-pointed star.

And it is the same seal the servants of God are sealed with in Revelation. So what is the seal we have to be sealed with? The law. The law. The law. There is nothing else to be said about it; if you keep pushing that star, that is your own vain opinion. Brothers and sisters, come on one accord and stop following the so-called white man and his lies.

precepts.label: Revelation 7:3-4
precepts.why:
“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Then jump up to verse 3: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

What is the seal talking about? Go right back to Isaiah 8:16: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The servants of God are sealed in their foreheads with the law, the same place Deuteronomy said the words of God would be “as frontlets between your eyes”, in the mind. Some are still saying the star of Moloch, the star of David; that is simple.

So the seal of Song of Solomon 8:6, set upon the heart and upon the arm, is the seal of the servants of God in Revelation: the law, laid up in the mind of the tribes of the children of Israel.

thread.label: Isaiah 9:6-7
thread.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: John 14:8-9
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the son that is given “The everlasting Father.” Most Christians, and even some Israelites, cannot explain that, because they have not figured out that the everlasting Father in the Old Testament was Christ. They say we always spoke to the Father. No, you did not speak to the Father; you spoke to Christ. That is why he is called the everlasting Father. John 14 is a precept for it.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” See Christ’s response: “Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?”

Yes, Christ looks like his Father. But what is he actually telling Philip? I created you. I am your Father, your everlasting Father. You were brought forth through me.

Remember, Christ is the only begotten of the Father. That means the Father created only Christ, and then told Christ to create everything else. So when Isaiah names the child born unto us “The mighty God, The everlasting Father”, it is because everything that exists was brought forth through him. That is why Philip, who had been with him so long, should have known him.

precepts.label: John 1:1-3
precepts.why:
In case anyone is still confused about why Christ is called “The everlasting Father”, John 1 settles it. We have to shake the Christian thoughts.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Christ was in the beginning with God, and he was God. “The same was in the beginning with God.” God is a plural there.

Then the part that matters: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ, and without Christ was not any thing made that was made. The Father only begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created.

That is why he said to Philip, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” I created all of this. That is too heavy for a Negro, because you have Baptist on your mind and Catholic in your head. It was hard for us in the beginning too, but the Most High has shown us. Let it marinate.

So the child born and the son given in Isaiah 9:6, with the government upon his shoulder, is the same one who made all things: the Word, the mighty God, the everlasting Father.

precepts.label: Matthew 13:31-32
precepts.why:
“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Christ explains that increase in Matthew 13: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.” If you grew up in the city you may not know what a mustard seed looks like; it is one of the smallest of all seeds.

“but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.” When it is grown: that is the increase of his government. It starts small. What we have here is small. We may think we have a lot, but this is nothing yet; we are still at the mustard seed stage.

And the kingdom of heaven is a government, not a church group. That is why it behooves us to learn God’s laws, commandments and statutes: to set up a government you need everything that makes a community, and God’s laws are going to filter everything for us. Right now we think small. God says think bigger. A house? Bigger. Property? Bigger. The world is ours, and for the world to be ours we have to be able to set all of that up.

Think how the Most High uses something as small as the human mind. As a man thinketh, so is he. Everything you lay your eyes on, every object and invention, was a thought first. We shortchange ourselves with doubt, but that is not what God made. Untapped greatness is waiting to bud; remove the doubt and the fear and let the Lord work on that head.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:12-21
precepts.why:
The mustard seed government is small now, and we think small. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” Solomon learned wisdom and gave it out freely, and that is what we are doing today: we don’t hide the riches of the wisdom of God. “For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.” If we use this wisdom we become the friends of God. And it comes from learning, not once but daily; that is what the classes every day are about.

“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements.” You might say you know how the world was made. You don’t: what elements make the air, what elements were made for the sun? Solomon understood that. He knew “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”, from Adam to the second coming of Christ. He knew “the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons”, “The circuits of years, and the positions of stars.”

“The natures of living creatures”: Esau puts cameras on animals, even in their butts, to learn how they defecate, trying to get on Solomon’s level with all that freakiness. Solomon knew “the furies of wild beasts”, “the violence of winds”, the tornadoes and storms, “the reasonings of men”, “the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”, which herb is for what, and “all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

We are not even on Solomon’s level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, and when he does we will be on that level and greater. That is what the mustard seed is about: we start small and it grows. This is the beginning of that government.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:5-6
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the government shall be upon his shoulder, “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice.” Jeremiah says the same: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch.” That righteous Branch is Christ.

“and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” See what he is going to do: execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations don’t want that. Some of us in here may not want that either: I don’t want no justice and judgment, hell no. Yes, it is coming anyway.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

So the throne of David in Isaiah 9 is the reign of this King, the Branch raised unto David. The increase of his government is a kingdom of judgment and justice, of law and order, and in his days Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely. That is why we learn God’s laws now: it is the government we are going to live under.

precepts.label: Psalms 74:2
precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” God has not changed the subject from Babylon; he changed the metaphor. Babylon, Lucifer, America: the same thing. America weakens all the nations.

“I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”: that is space travel. “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”: that is slavery. When you are sitting on somebody, you have conquered them, you beat them. Well, who is the congregation? Is it the church, the Baptist church, the Catholic church?

“Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old; the rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed; this mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.”

The congregation is the people God purchased of old, the rod of his inheritance, the people he redeemed, mount Zion where he dwelt. That is Israel. So when Lucifer says he will sit upon the mount of the congregation, he is saying he will sit on God’s own inheritance, and that is what was done to us in the sides of the north, North America.

precepts.label: Exodus 12:47
precepts.why:
To prove who the congregation is, one more: “All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.”

That is it right there. The congregation is Israel. Not the church, not the Baptist church, not the Catholic church: the congregation of Israel, the ones commanded to keep the passover.

So read Isaiah again: “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation”: that is Israel. “in the sides of the north”: that is North America. “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds”: that is airplanes and helicopters. “I will be like the most High”: I will be like God. “Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.” Regardless of all the technological power they have, America, Babylon, Lucifer is going to be brought down to hell.

And he is the one “that opened not the house of his prisoners”. We are the prisoners, the congregation he sat on, but our people believe they are free.

precepts.label: Ephesians 2:20
precepts.why:
Against the covenant with death, the Lord God lays something else: “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.” This stone is Christ, and Ephesians proves it: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.”

Christ himself is the chief corner stone. That means he is the leader; he is the commander. Everyone else has built on something else. Our people made a covenant with death, the white man and his philosophies, and an agreement with hell, keeping our people in a low state. They made lies their refuge, Christianity and democracy, and hid themselves under falsehood, thinking the overflowing scourge of judgment will not come to them. precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:5-8
precepts.why:
Habakkuk draws the spoiler of Isaiah 33:1 line by line. “Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine”: this white man transgresses by wine, and his wine is his philosophies, his falsehoods, his political policies and his religions. “he is a proud man”: you don't get no prouder than this white man, in particular Donald Trump. “neither keepeth at home”: America don't keep at home; he's in everybody's business. What are you doing in Venezuela? What are you doing over there in Iran?

“who enlargeth his desire as hell”: wherever he goes he sets up democracy, and that country, city or state goes to hell, a low state. God says he “is as death, and cannot be satisfied”. He steals one thing and still ain't satisfied; now he wants Denmark, and says he should take Canada too. God is showing us this man's attributes. He “gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people”: America is the great melting pot, all nations, languages and tongues are here.

“Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long?” All these are the remnants from the destabilized, bombed and devastated countries, and they are here now. The oil in Venezuela is not his, the riches in Iran are not his, the riches of Libya he took; when he put sanctions on Russia they seized Russia's boats and all the wealth Putin had in American places, and nobody says nothing. How long is this going to go on? The thick clay he ladeth himself with is the nations he has all around him, the ones that come to live in America and say, I love Donald.

“Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee”: awake from sleep, because they are sleeper cells from the nations he destroyed. They bombed Nigeria, and you got Nigerians here; they bombed Somalia, and you got a whole lot of Somalis here; Yemen, and you got Yemenites; they've been hitting Iran, and a lot of Iranians live in the United States.

“Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee; because of men’s blood”. You murdered civilians, innocent men, innocent women, innocent children. You killed my mother, my father, my son, my daughter: that's how you make a terrorist. The first thing they bombed in Iran was a school full of little girls ages 5 to 10. Their mothers and fathers are screaming and crying, their relatives here are asking what happened to their little cousins, and there's no forgiveness for that. They are not going to let bygones be bygones.

That is Isaiah 33:1 fulfilled: the one that spoiled and was not spoiled shall be spoiled, by the very remnant of the nations he robbed.

precepts.label: Micah 2:11
precepts.why:
“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” This defines the wine of Habakkuk 2:5. Wine is a metaphor for the spirit of falsehood and lies.

That is the one in Isaiah 33:1 that spoils and deals treacherously: proud, in everybody's business, setting up his democracy wherever he goes. Isaiah 33:1 says woe to him, because when he ceases to spoil, he shall be spoiled.

precepts.label: 1 Thessalonians 5:3
precepts.why:
The New Testament speaks of the same thing. “For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them”. They are going to think it's all good: we have subdued the earth, everything is ours. And the Lord says no; when you say that, then comes sudden destruction.

“as travail upon a woman with child” means birthing pains. One thing may happen today, it may calm down, and two to three months later something else happens, or it might be two to three years later. It comes like a woman giving birth. “and they shall not escape.”

That is the end of Isaiah 33:1: “when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee.” When America stops robbing countries, it is going to be robbed; the nations shall deal treacherously with it, and it will come right when it says peace and safety.

precepts.label: Job 20:22-23
precepts.why:
“In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits”. When he is full, because he did all the destruction and robbed the nations, he shall be in straits, meaning he is going to catch hell. This is talking about the same thing as Isaiah 33:1.

“every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.” We read that in Habakkuk 2, where all the remnant of the people shall spoil him, and you can read it in Revelation 17, when NATO turns on them, because it is going to happen.

“When he is about to fill his belly, God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain it upon him while he is eating.” That is the same thing Thessalonians said: when they say peace and safety, sudden destruction.

They are trying to make it look like we are the bad guys. But the real bad guys are written in the Bible, and it is the people they are friends with now, the other nations and their own people, that are going to turn on them and attack them. The Lord told us to wait upon him till the day that he rises up. We trust in our God.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 9:24
precepts.why:
“O Lord, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee”: that is our prayer, just like Hezekiah prayed. We have to wait on the Lord. “The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.”

Jeremiah 9:24 shows what Israel glories in: “But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the Lord which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the Lord.” That is what we have to glory in, brothers: that we understand and know the Lord.

All nations do not understand and know the Lord, so they do not glory in the Lord. The judgment and righteousness the Lord delights to exercise in the earth are the same judgment and righteousness he has filled Zion with. Knowing him is Israel's glory, while the nations are scattered at the lifting up of himself.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:5
precepts.why:
How has the Lord “filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”? Jeremiah 23:5: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.”

This righteous Branch is Christ. He is the King who shall reign and prosper, and he is the one who executes judgment and justice in the earth. So when Isaiah 33:5 says “The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”, it is through Christ, the King, the King of kings.

That is our hope amid destruction. When the Lord rises up, the nations are scattered and their spoil is gathered like the gathering of the caterpillar, and the righteous Branch of David reigns over Zion with judgment and justice.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:28
precepts.why:
“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times.” Why is that important? The wisdom and knowledge of this Bible keeps us mentally and spiritually stable. Deuteronomy 28:28 shows the opposite: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.”

Madness: our people are crazy, mentally unstable, mentally insane. Blindness: we are spiritually blind. Astonishment of heart: our people are always shocked at what is going on in the world.

That is the curse that wisdom answers. Brothers, we all need the wisdom of God and the knowledge to keep us mentally and spiritually stable. The people who know the Bible are not shocked when these things happen, because the Bible already said it; the people without it are astonished at every turn.

precepts.label: Sirach 19:20
precepts.why:
“the fear of the Lord is his treasure.” Sirach 19:20 says “The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.”

So the fear of the Lord is all wisdom. Brothers and sisters, if you don't fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

And in all wisdom is the performance of the law: the application of God's law. We must not just talk about it; we must be about it. We must do it. The wisdom and knowledge that are the stability of our times are not only words in the head; they are the law performed, joined to the knowledge of his omnipotency. That is the treasure the Lord loves.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 2:14
precepts.why:
Wisdom and knowledge are the stability of our times. 2 Peter 2:14 is the flip side of that, what it looks like when your life is not stable and your mind is not saturated with the word of God: “Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children.”

Our people have eyes full of adultery and cannot cease from sin. They beguile unstable souls, the ones without the stability of the word. Our people are cursed children.

Many of us have children, and we all want them to walk right with the Lord. We train them up the best we can, just like the prophet Samuel, yet Samuel's sons went to hell off. Be mindful, especially the women: you have to know the spirits in your children. You are going to find out which ones serve the Lord and which ones don't.

precepts.label: James 1:5-9
precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If any of you are dumb as a rock, ask of God. Some do not have the spirit of discernment: they see right and wrong in front of them and cannot discern it. When judgment is passed there is always that one who asks why a brother or sister had to be put out of the school when all they did was commit a little adultery. Shut up and sit down; they cannot discern. So pray, as Hezekiah laid his prayer before the Lord: pray for wisdom, knowledge and the spirit of discernment.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” And give the Lord something to work with. You cannot sit at the table with a chicken leg in one hand and a steak in the other praying, Lord, help me lose weight. Likewise you pray for wisdom but the Bible is closed Sunday through Friday and opened only on the Sabbath. The views on the classes peak on Saturday and nobody watches the rest of the week, the same as Christians on Sunday. Many are called, few are chosen; this is for the chosen few that know what to do.

“For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: not some of his ways, all of them. Reading once a week leaves nothing for the Lord to work with.

“Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted.” That brother is studying, reading and praying, Lord help my understanding, even when he does not understand yet. The quiet brother who did not do much talking years back becomes the one breaking down what the scriptures mean. If reading hurts your eyes, put on Bible audio at night and wake up to the scriptures.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:40
precepts.why:
When the books of Jerusalem were burned, the Lord told Ezra not to worry, and gave him the cup: “And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory.”

That last part is the point. God needed something to work with. The Spirit had to access Ezra's memory so that he could rewrite the records. It is like the movie Limitless: the pill opened his memory all the way back, so he could remember things he had only glanced at.

So if you do not read the Bible except on the Sabbath and you pray, Lord, open my wisdom, the Spirit comes and there is nothing in there: no memory to access and bring to your mind. Wisdom and knowledge can only be the stability of your times if the word has been put in you first, so give the Lord something to work with.

precepts.label: Sirach 11:12
precepts.why:
For the brother who says he has a reading impediment, or that his eyes hurt: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” This is a brother who is mentally slow, lacking ability, and poor.

“yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate”. The Lord lifted his head from misery, so that many who saw it marveled. It is the same as James's brother of low degree who rejoices that he is exalted.

So it is not impossible, but give the Lord something to work with. Show him that you believe and have faith, and he can do wonders. If you want to lose weight, get in the gym, eat smaller portions, walk around the block once, then twice, and let the Lord do the rest. Instead of five pieces of chicken, eat one; you won't die. In the same way, put on Bible audio if reading is hard. Do your part and the eye of the Lord will look upon you for good.

precepts.label: Luke 21:24-28
precepts.why:
Luke 21 shows people who are unstable in all their ways, wavering like the waves of the sea. “And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars”: eclipses of the sun, lunar eclipses, what they call blood moons. “and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity”: we are living in that time now. Perplexity means confusion. They said Venezuela was drug dealers, as they did with Manuel Noriega; they said Iraq had weapons of mass destruction and did not find one bomb. Anytime white people say it is a complex issue, it is something very easy that they don't want you to know: Maduro was selling his oil in foreign currencies, not the United States dollar; Iran was doing the same; Gaddafi wanted to.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth.” Why are they afraid? We are not afraid, because wisdom and knowledge are the stability of our times: this is what the Bible was talking about, while everybody else is confused. “for the powers of heaven shall be shaken”: America, England, France, Germany.

“And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” It is going to be almost time to go home.

But there is more to the one word perplexity: it goes into Jacob's trouble, the great tribulation that comes to try us. People want to skip the tribulation and say, war, Christ might come back tomorrow. No he won't. Jacob's trouble has to come to pass first.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:29-31
precepts.why:
Christ says it himself: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days.” People say there is no tribulation; there is going to be tribulation. Then “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”, as Luke read, “and the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles. “and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: America, Britain, Germany, France, Russia, Canada, Spain, all those European nations, shaken with war.

How do we know the heavens are those nations? Isaiah 34: “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine”: bombs, nuclear bombs, missiles and satellites dropping out of the sky. “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea.” Idumea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom: America, France, Germany, Britain, Russia. That is heaven.

“And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven.” After the tribulation there is still war; so don't say there's war, we're going home tomorrow. Where is the great tribulation, Jacob's trouble?

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds.” He is not gathering everybody, only the elect: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” The elect are the Israelites, not Baptists, Pentecostals, Muslims or Catholics. That is our hope amid destruction.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:5
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33 ends: “And the people shall be as the burnings of lime: as thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire.” There is going to be fire, but it is not the kind of fire we read about in 2 Kings, men being burnt up with fire from heaven in that way. Isaiah 9 shows what kind of fire it is.

precepts.label: Daniel 9:7
precepts.why:
“Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.” Who are the far off? Daniel shows it's us.

“O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day.” The literal example: we were the top nation. Nations paid tribute to us under Solomon; David conquered everybody. Then we went into captivity, confused, and it was our sins that allowed it.

Bring it up to today. Our people go to school, get educated, get many degrees, and still are not accepted in this society. I assimilated, master, I'm one of you. That is confusion of faces.

“To the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them.” Look at our people: Dominicans and Cubans saying I voted for Donald Trump, and now it is backfiring on them. precepts.label: Daniel 7:9-11
precepts.why:
“Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?” What does it mean to dwell with fire? Daniel shows what it is to stand before the Lord in his kingdom.

“I beheld till the thrones were cast down.” Daniel looked in the vision and saw America fall, Britain, Germany, France, Canada and Australia fall, and China, Japan, North Korea and South Korea: all the powerful nations. “And the Ancient of days did sit”: having no beginning of days and no end of days, and in order to sit, you have to have a body. “Whose garment was white as snow”: to wear a garment you have to have a body. “And the hair of his head like the pure wool.” So what is God? A black man.

“His throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.” His wheels are the chariots of heaven that they call UFOs. “A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him”: fire bursting from the throne at all times. You are not just rolling up on the Lord saying, Lord, I want to talk to you for a minute. You have to get through that fire first. This is going to be a kingdom of absolute order and rule.

“Thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened. I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame.” The horn speaking great words and the beast is America, slain and given to the burning flame.

That is the devouring fire and the everlasting burnings of Isaiah 33. The sinners in Zion are afraid of it, and only he that walketh righteously and speaketh uprightly shall dwell there.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:16-17
precepts.why:
“The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites.” Zion is another name for Israel, and fearfulness will surprise the hypocrites of our people. Isaiah 9 gives the example.

“For the leaders of this people cause them to err.” These are the religious leaders and the political leaders of our people. Our leaders in this society cause us to err, cause us to sin, because we follow what they say and it is always against God. “And they that are led of them are destroyed.” You followed T.D. Jakes? You followed Pastor P and the other dudes on the screen? Destroyed.

“Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men.” Because they follow foolish religious leaders and foolish political leaders. “Neither shall have mercy on their fatherless and widows”: God is not going to have mercy on the fatherless children and the widows whose husbands died.

“For every one is an hypocrite and an evildoer, and every mouth speaketh folly.” Every one of them is a hypocrite. They all have the Bible, they say they believe in Jesus, but they won't do nary a word in that book. Every mouth speaks lies; as soon as they open their black lips, it's a lie, and it isn't in the scriptures. “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.”

Look at the churches: holy water and holy kisses, people falling out saying they have the Holy Spirit. That is why the racist white man says all the Black churches need to be shut down and come learn from the white man how to serve God. And now there are Israelites who know they are Israel speaking in tongues and calling it a heavenly language, bringing the lies of foolishness into this truth. Those are the hypocrites the fear will surprise.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:2-5
precepts.why:
When the Bible calls our people hypocrites, look at the hypocrisy. “Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.” Christ was condemning the Pharisees, who gave their alms publicly and made a big announcement that they gave such an amount of money so everybody could see.

“But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.”

Now look at Marvin Winans at Perfecting Church. A grandmother stands up to sow her seed of a thousand plus two hundred thirty-five dollars before everybody, and he embarrasses her: y'all not listening, I said a thousand plus a thousand. She says she'll work on the other eight hundred, and he says that ain't what I asked you to do, and the organ goes right on playing like it agreed. That is what the Pharisees were doing, sounding a trumpet in the synagogue.

“And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.” And there are thousands praying in the streets in California to be seen: that is what Christ said not to do. Those are all Christians.

The Pharisees were our people, and the hypocrites of Isaiah 33 whom fearfulness will surprise are our people in these churches today, doing the very things Christ condemned.

precepts.label: Matthew 23:14
precepts.why:
“Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.” Christ is talking about the Pharisees being hypocrites, and the Pharisees were our people, devouring widows' houses.

She only found out because the treasurer went back to thank the donor, and the donor said, no, that money was for them. Now there is a big falling out, and the pastor is trying to force the widow out of the church. These pastors are robbing widows. That is what Christ said the Pharisees do, and he is telling us, don't do that.

And their end: the unfaithful servant is cut asunder and given “his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” That is the lake of fire when the Lord returns.

In that time he was talking about the Pharisees, but today the modern-day Pharisees are our people in Christianity. They do everything the Pharisees did. Those are the hypocrites Isaiah says fearfulness will surprise, when they ask who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire.
