precepts.label: Isaiah 2:2-3
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:16 says the one who walks righteously “shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks”. His place of defence is the kingdom, and Isaiah 2 shows what the munitions of rocks are.

“And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills”. The mountain of the Lord's house is the highest government on earth, literally. “and all nations shall flow unto it.”

“And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law”. That is what goes forth out of Zion: the law.

So to dwell on high is to dwell in that kingdom, set above every other government, and that is the promise to the one who meets the stipulation of Isaiah 33:15. There, “bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure.”

precepts.label: Revelation 19:16
precepts.why:
“And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.” When Isaiah 33:17 says “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty”, it is talking about Christ. He is the King of kings; he is the Lord of lords.

Isaiah 33 asks who shall dwell with the devouring fire, who shall dwell with everlasting burnings before the Lord, and answers: he that walketh righteously and speaketh uprightly, speaking what the Bible says and living what it says; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, the oppression you see as soon as you walk out these doors, which our brothers and sisters in the church make like they don't see; he that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes; he that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil. That one shall dwell on high.

And that one shall see the King. We want to see the Lord for ourselves, and the King we shall see in his beauty is Christ, with his name written on his vesture and on his thigh.

precepts.label: Job 19:25-27
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:17 says “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty”, and Job shows how. “For I know that my redeemer liveth”. Our redeemer is Christ, who sacrificed himself for our people, the twelve tribes of Israel. “and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth”: in the latter day our redeemer shall stand upon the earth.

“And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God”. Job said, after my death, when worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God. He knew he would be resurrected, regenerated, and we have to know that thing too. Although you die, you are going to be resurrected and regenerated, and that is when your eyes shall see the King in his beauty.

“Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another”. It is not going to be somebody else, and it is not only spiritual, as the Christians say, because Christians don't know the Bible. Job said, I'm going to be back for myself, and I'm going to behold the Lord with my own eyes, and not another, “though my reins be consumed within me”: though my body be destroyed.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 46:27
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:17 ends, “they shall behold the land that is very far off”, and that land is Jerusalem. Jeremiah shows how we get back to it.

“But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel”. He says it because of great tribulation: Jacob's trouble will be coming. Tribulation leads into Armageddon. World War III has already begun, and in the middle of that will be Armageddon. So the Lord says, fear not, be not dismayed.

“for, behold, I will save thee from afar off”, because we have been taken captive into far off lands; here in America is a far off land. “and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and be in rest and at ease”. We ain't going to be bothered by anybody; we shall be in rest and at ease. “and none shall make him afraid”: there is no nation that is going to make us afraid ever, ever again.

So the one whose eyes see the King in his beauty is also brought out of the far off land of his captivity to behold the land that is very far off, Jerusalem, and dwell there in rest.

thread.label: Isaiah 33:18-20
thread.text: Thine heart shall meditate terror. Where is the scribe? where is the receiver? where is he that counted the towers?

classes.title: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.label: Isaiah 25:3-5
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people”, and Isaiah 25 shows why: those fierce nations will be subdued. “Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee.” The terrible nations, the ones that made everyone afraid, will themselves fear the Most High.

“For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.” That is us. Verse 4 is Israel: the poor and the needy that the terrible ones have been blasting against like a storm, and God has been our refuge through it.

“Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers”, and that goes right back to verse 3: the city of the terrible nations shall fear. Then, “the branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low”: their branch, their people, brought low. So when Isaiah 33 says we shall not see that fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue, it is because God has brought them down.

precepts.label: Revelation 15:4
precepts.why:
“Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest.” His judgments made manifest are his prophecies and his laws coming to pass before everyone's eyes.

This is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” When all nations come and worship before the Most High, they are no longer fierce against Israel. They are subdued. That is what the Lord is saying here: these nations will be brought down and made to come and worship before him.

So the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue, the nations whose languages we cannot understand, will not be seen raging against us any more. They will be bowing before the King, because the Lord only is holy and all the nations will fear him.

precepts.label: Zechariah 14:16
precepts.why:
Zechariah shows what it looks like when the nations are subdued: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

Those that are left are the ones who came against Jerusalem. These nations are going to be forced to give up their idols and come before the King. Year after year they must go up and keep the feast of tabernacles, the very feast they never kept.

That is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” The fierce nations with a stammering tongue will not be fierce any more; what is left of them will be worshipping the King, the Lord of hosts, at Jerusalem.

precepts.label: Psalms 9:19-20
precepts.why:
“Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail”: let not man prevail against us. Then, “let the heathen be judged in thy sight”: let the heathen nations be judged in his sight. “Put them in fear, O Lord: that the nations may know themselves to be but men.” These nations must learn that they themselves are only men. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

Then read Isaiah 33:19 again: “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” Why? Because they shall be subdued. It is “a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand”: that is the other nations, whose languages we do not know.

The nations have acted like gods over Israel. The Most High puts them in fear so they know they are but men, and then they are subdued and forced to worship the King. That is why we will not see that fierce people again.

precepts.label: Psalms 46:4-7
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:20 says to look upon Zion and see Jerusalem “a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down”. Habitation meaning at rest, at peace. Like a tent with stakes driven down, not one stake of Jerusalem shall ever be pulled up, and not one cord broken.

Psalms 46 says the same: “There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High. God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.”

“The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved”: all the heathen nations, the same ones we read about in Isaiah 33:19, the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue that we cannot understand. Their kingdoms shall be moved. And “he uttered his voice, the earth melted. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.” God is our refuge; it is true.

So the nations are moved, but Jerusalem is not. She shall not be moved, because God is in the midst of her.

precepts.label: Psalms 48:1-2
precepts.why:
“Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.” The mountain of his holiness is Jerusalem.

“Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.” This is the Zion that Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon: “Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities.” It is the city of the great King, the joy of the whole earth.

So the quiet habitation Isaiah saw is not a small thing. It is the city where the Lord is greatly praised, beautiful for situation, and it will never be taken down again.

precepts.label: Psalms 122:1-5
precepts.why:
“I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.” That should make you glad. When somebody says, let's go up to the sanctuary, and you sigh, there is something wrong with your spirit. “Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem.”

“Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”: the same height and the same width. Revelation 21 shows it: the city lieth foursquare, the length and the breadth and the height of it equal, measured by the angel, its foundations garnished with the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28, the stones with the names of the twelve tribes.

“Whither the tribes go up.” Wait a minute. Where all nations go up? No: whither the tribes go up, “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord.” The testimony of Israel, because that kingdom is what was always prophesied. The kingdom is not for everybody.

“For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Luke 22:30 shows those thrones, sitting on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel, and Revelation 20:4 shows who sits on them: the souls beheaded for the witness of Jesus, who had not worshipped the beast, the white man's kingdom, nor his image, his religion and his politics, nor received his mark, his lies in their foreheads, their minds. They live and reign with Christ a thousand years. This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:12-21
precepts.why:
Psalms 122 says “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”, and Revelation 21 shows what that means: “the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth”, measured “with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” It is as tall as it is wide.

Twelve thousand furlongs is about 1,500 miles by man's measurement, but it is not man's measurement: “according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” It is angelic measurement, so the size is not what we are thinking.

And “the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass. And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones.” Garnished means decorated: all kinds of fancy designs in the walls of Jerusalem. Jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprasus, jacinth, amethyst. Each stone represented one of the tribes, the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28. “And the twelve gates were twelve pearls”, “and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass.”

And the city “had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” So the kingdom is not for everybody. This is the Zion Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon, the tabernacle that shall never be taken down.

precepts.label: Exodus 28:15-21
precepts.why:
The foundations of the kingdom of heaven are the same stones, the same gems, that the high priest wore. “And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment with cunning work”: cunning work means make it look fancy. It has to be dope; it has to look good, not corny. It is made “of gold, of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine twined linen, shalt thou make it.”

“Foursquare it shall be being doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof.” It was designed like a square, the same height as it was wide, just like the kingdom, where the length and the breadth and the height are equal.

“And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones”: sardius, topaz and carbuncle; emerald, sapphire and diamond; ligure, agate and amethyst; beryl, onyx and jasper. And “they shall be set in gold in their inclosings”, the gold holding them in.

“And the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet; every one with his name shall they be according to the twelve tribes.” These stones are the names of the children of Israel. Revelation 21 says the same thing about the kingdom of heaven: its foundations and its gates carry the twelve tribes. The Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20 is built on Israel.

precepts.label: Luke 22:30
precepts.why:
Psalms 122:5 says “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles where those thrones are: “That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

The thrones in Jerusalem are thrones for judging the twelve tribes. That is why Psalms 122 says it is whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, and not all nations.

So the quiet habitation of Isaiah 33:20, the city of our solemnities, is the seat of the kingdom, with Christ's table and the thrones of the house of David set in it.

precepts.label: Revelation 20:4
precepts.why:
“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”: the thrones of judgment of Psalms 122.

Then “I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: that is great tribulation. They are the ones “which had not worshipped the beast”: which had not worshipped this white man, this kingdom. Nor “his image”: his religion, his politics. And they had not “received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: they did not receive his lies in their foreheads, in their minds.

And so “they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” Those who come through great tribulation without bowing to the beast are the ones who sit on the thrones in the Jerusalem Isaiah 33:20 describes, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

precepts.label: Psalms 68:22-30
precepts.why:
“The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring my people again from the depths of the sea.” Why bring them again? Because God's people are not in the holy land. “That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies, and the tongue of thy dogs in the same.” Damn! Our foot shall be dipped in the blood of our enemies, and those nations that run their mouths against us, the same with them.

“They have seen thy goings, O God; even the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.” That is the sanctuary. “The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels.” People singing before the Lord, not like these churches: beautiful songs, with men and women behind them playing instruments and young girls with timbrels. “Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.” The fountain of Israel is Christ.

“There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.” Little Benjamin because they almost got wiped out, and they are the youngest tribe, the baby tribe. This is his re-established kingdom.

“Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents unto thee”: tribute. “Rebuke the company of spearmen”, the soldiers, “the multitude of the bulls”, the people that have power in the other nations, “with the calves of the people”, their little ones, “till every one submit himself with pieces of silver”: till every nation submits and brings us tribute. Then, “scatter thou the people that delight in war.” You know who that is? The white man. If there is no war, he will make one; if there is peace on earth, he will undo it. They changed the Department of Defense to the Department of War. They delight in war.

This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20: the temple standing, the tribes gathered, the kings bringing tribute, and the fierce nations subdued.

precepts.label: Psalms 140:1-5
precepts.why:
Psalms 140 proves who the people are that delight in war. “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man.” Psalms 68 said scatter the nations that delight in war; don't you see Trump and them delighting in war?

“Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” You thought it would end with Venezuela. Oh, no. He said we are going to hit Iran. You thought it ended there; next week Mexico, and maybe Cuba. The party is not over.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent”: the things they say. Don't you hear them mocking the nations? They wanted to land in Spain, Spain said no, and now they are mad and talking about Spain. And “adders’ poison is under their lips”: their philosophies, their religions, their politics. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”: this so-called white man, keep me from their hands. Then, “preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” They purposed to overthrow the goings of the children of Israel. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me. Selah.” Traps all around.

These are the fierce nations of Isaiah 33:19. When the Lord scatters them, we shall not see that fierce people any more, and Jerusalem will be a quiet habitation.

precepts.label: Psalms 60:7
precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.” The Lord is our judge, not the nations. And the Lord is our lawgiver. Brothers used to get confused over this, so David shows which tribe the lawgiver comes from: “Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the strength of mine head; Judah is my lawgiver”.

You would think it is supposed to be Levi, the priestly tribe. It says Judah. Why? Because the Lord who is our lawgiver came out of Judah, as Hebrews 7:14 shows. Christ is the lawgiver: he is the one that gave Moses the laws, and he is from Judah.

precepts.label: Hebrews 7:14
precepts.why:
Psalm 60 says “Judah is my lawgiver”, when you would expect it to say Levi. Hebrews gives the reason: “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.”

So Christ is the lawgiver. He comes from the tribe of Judah, and he is the one that gave Moses the laws. That is the Lord Isaiah speaks of: “the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us.” Our judge, our lawgiver and our king is Christ out of Judah, and it is he who will save us when the warships and navies of the nations come down.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 31:7-9
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “then is the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame take the prey.” Who is the lame? Jeremiah shows it: “For thus saith the Lord; Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations: publish ye, praise ye, and say, O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel.” The Lord is not saving all Israelites; he is saving a remnant.

“Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth, and with them the blind and the lame”. The blind and the lame are Israel, with “the woman with child and her that travaileth with child together: a great company shall return thither.”

“They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.” Ephraim is the firstborn, meaning he was chosen over the northern kingdom.

So the lame that take the prey is Israel. When the tacklings of their ships are loosed and they cannot spread the sail, we are going to take the nations: we are going to prey on the nations.

precepts.label: Matthew 15:31
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “the lame take the prey. And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick”. Jeremiah 31 showed the lame is Israel, and Christ shows the lame being made whole: “Insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel.”

The dumb speak, the maimed are whole, the lame walk and the blind see, and they glorified the God of Israel. That is the lame of Isaiah 33. The lame take the prey: we are going to take the nations and divide the spoil, and in that day the inhabitants of Jerusalem will never say, I am sick.

precepts.label: Psalms 103:1-4
precepts.why:
Isaiah ends, “And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity.” Nobody is going to be saying they are sick. David shows why: “Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits”.

Watch the benefits: “Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies”. The same Lord who forgives all our iniquities heals all our diseases, and the Lord can redeem our life from destruction.

That is the hope amid destruction. While the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations and his fury upon all their armies, the people that dwell in Jerusalem are forgiven their iniquity and healed, never to say I am sick again.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 8:56
precepts.why:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail”. We must all get into the habit of consistently reading, four chapters a day minimum, because not one prophecy in it shall fail. Solomon witnessed it at the dedication of the temple:

“Blessed be the Lord, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.”

Not one word failed of what he promised by Moses, and not one word shall fail of what he promised by Isaiah. The same God who gave Israel rest in the land according to all that he promised has promised the day of the Lord’s vengeance, “the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion”, the sword coming down upon Idumea and the great slaughter in the land of Edom. We are living the controversy of Zion now, with Amalek claiming the land is theirs.

None of the promises in this Bible shall fail. That is why we seek out of the book of the Lord and read: what he said by his prophets will come to pass just as surely as the rest he gave Israel in the days of Solomon.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:13-14
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”, and Paul tells Timothy the same thing: “Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.” Read, brothers and sisters. Give attendance to reading, to exhortation and to doctrine until Christ comes.

“Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery”: the presbytery is the congregation. Just as Timothy had the gift of the Holy Spirit within him, we all have the gift of the Holy Spirit within us. Don’t let anybody tell you that to show the gift you have to speak in tongues. John the Baptist had the gift of the Holy Spirit, anointed in his mother’s womb. Did John the Baptist speak in tongues? No. Stop listening to these Christians.

And what we read must be the book of the Lord alone. “none shall want her mate”: you cannot mate the Bible with any other book. Islam tries to do that, mixing the Quran with the Bible, and God says you cannot. “for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” God’s mouth commanded these words to be written and his spirit gathered them together; “he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line”. As he divided the land of Israel by line, he gave the prophets lines to write: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and David big portions, Obadiah, Micah, Amos, Jonah and Nahum small ones. “they shall possess it for ever”: as we will possess the land for ever, we will possess the word of God for ever, and we give attendance to reading it until he comes.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:20
precepts.why:
“Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the people be assembled: who among them can declare this, and shew us former things? let them bring forth their witnesses.” Who can show the things from the past? The next verse answers: “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen.” God’s witnesses on this earth are the children of Israel, and the two sticks, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, the southern and northern kingdoms, are two witnesses also.

What does a witness have? A testimony. A witness testifies, like a witness to a crime in a court of law. And we do not play a small role. Isaiah shows what God’s witnesses testify: “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

As witnesses, what we are supposed to be testifying is the law and the testimony. If they do not speak according to this word, the law and the testimony, there is no light in them.

The testimony is what John bore record of: “the testimony of Jesus Christ, and of all things that he saw.” Part of that testimony is to identify “them which say they are Jews, and are not”, the synagogue of Satan. And Malachi’s testimony: “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness.” The they who call them that are the witnesses, the prophets. So when the nations are gathered and asked for witnesses, Israel stands to the law and to the testimony.

precepts.label: Sirach 36:14
precepts.why:
“Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.” A witness has a testimony. What is the testimony Israel carries? Sirach shows where it came from: “Fill Sion with thine unspeakable oracles, and thy people with thy glory: Give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in thy name.”

The testimonies are what God gave to Moses, to Jeremiah, to Nahum, to Micah, to Isaiah, to Peter, Paul and the apostles. All the things these men wrote are the testimony: testimonies of things that are going to happen in the future, of what is going to happen to the children of Israel.

So when the scripture says the witnesses have to testify, the testimony is what is written, what the prophets said is going to happen. That is why Isaiah 43:9 asks “who among them can declare this, and shew us former things?” No other nation can. Israel, the people God possessed from the beginning, was given the unspeakable oracles, and we testify them.

And as we testify, we bring forth judgment. Brought before governors and kings “for a testimony against them and the Gentiles”, it is not we who speak but the Spirit of our Father speaking in us. The wicked who hides as an angel of light is revealed and condemned, because the witnesses must testify first before God brings forth judgment, as in a court of law.

precepts.label: Revelation 3:9
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the kings and queens of the nations “shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet.” Christ says the same thing in Revelation: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet.”

Those that say they are Jews and are not, but do lie, will be made to come and worship before the feet of the true Israel. That is the bowing down. Before thy feet in Revelation is with their face toward the earth, licking up the dust of thy feet, in Isaiah. The two scriptures say the same thing.

We can hardly fathom these words right now. Who is going to bow down in front of the black man? People will look at it and say you are dreaming. But guess what? That is what the scripture says. Let God be true, and every man a liar.

So don’t worry about the hatred, and don’t worry about what we are going through here. Christ is coming to save us from the hand of all that hate us, and what we have coming is greater: the Lord lifts up his hand to the Gentiles, they bring Israel’s sons in their arms and carry her daughters upon their shoulders, and “thou shalt know that I am the Lord: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.”

thread.text: He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.

classes.title: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.label: John 19:14-16
precepts.why:
We might think that Christ doesn't understand what we are going through. Isaiah 53 shows that Christ knows perfectly well what we are going through. The whole chapter is talking about Christ, and verse 8 says: “He was taken from prison and from judgment.” How?

John shows it. “And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cesar’s friend.” Pilate “brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.”

“And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King! But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar. Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.”

That is how he was taken from prison and from judgment: bound, set before the judgment seat, rejected by his own for Caesar, and led away. The one who was taken from prison is the one who comes to preach to our people, who are in the prison house today.

precepts.label: Psalms 22:30-31
precepts.why:
“and who shall declare his generation?” David answers: “A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation. They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this.”

To declare means to teach. To declare means to preach. They shall come and shall declare his righteousness: that's us, you and me. Unto a people that shall be born: that's us too.

So the question Isaiah asks is answered by a seed that serves him and is accounted to the Lord for a generation. Christ was cut off out of the land of the living, but his generation is declared by those who come after, teaching and preaching his righteousness to our people that he hath done this.

precepts.label: Daniel 9:26
precepts.why:
“for he was cut off out of the land of the living”: that is when he was crucified. Daniel prophesied it: “And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself.” Messiah, that's Christ, is cut off, but not for himself. He didn't die for himself; Isaiah says, “for the transgression of my people was he stricken.”

“and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.” The people of the prince that shall come is Rome.

So the same Rome that dominated Israel when Christ was cut off came and destroyed the city and the sanctuary. Christ was cut off for the transgression of his people, and desolations were determined upon the city by the hand of Rome.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:28
precepts.why:
“For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity.” Our hands in the black and brown community are defiled with blood. In Joliet a young man, twenty-three years old, shot to death his own mother, his aunt, his uncle, his bedridden brother and his three sisters, killed another man and shot one more, and then shot himself. That's trauma right there, and the law explains it: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.”

The Lord shall smite thee with madness: meaning our people are insane. No rhyme, no reason to what they do or why they do it. That's being smitten with madness. We have generational curses. Three teens on a thirty-hour spree of armed robberies and the murder of a churchgoing man; a woman charged with stabbing and killing a three-year-old boy, appearing in court laughing and smiling: that is stricken with madness.

The Bible says, thou shalt not kill, and we are not taught that in church, so some of us grow up with a hateful and murderous spirit on us. No matter how bad, insulting or degrading these videos are, they are filtered through the Bible, showing the stage and state of where we are today, and it is still proof that we are the children of Israel under the curses. The Bible ain't the white man's book. The Bible is our book.

That is why the Lord's hand is not shortened and his ear is not heavy, and still he does not save: “your iniquities have separated between you and your God.”

precepts.label: Revelation 13:9-10
precepts.why:
“None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth.” You might say, that's not right; our people are in the street all the time crying, no justice, no peace. But the justice our people want is called money. They don't want the justice of the Bible. Here is God's justice: “If any man have an ear, let him hear. He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.”

Now that's justice. And you know what our people say? No, you hate the white man. They know what the scripture means: the one who led into slavery going into slavery, the one who killed with the sword being put to death by the sword. And they say, no, we don't want that kind of justice. We want money, money, money.

That is Isaiah 59:4: none calling for God's justice. They cry for justice in the streets, but when the justice of God is read to them, they call it hateful.

precepts.label: Psalms 89:14
precepts.why:
“Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face.” God's throne is all about justice and judgment. That's exactly what the world doesn't want.

“nor any pleadeth for truth”: they are not pleading for God's truth. The families of our brothers and sisters put to death unjustly, Sandra Bland and the rest, want the truth regarding their case, but they don't want God's truth as a whole. We may march with them and support them, but there is no internal change: they are mad at the white man and still celebrating Christmas and the white man's holidays. “be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.” If I used to celebrate Easter, now I celebrate Passover. They are making a conscious effort not to change.

The Lord is coming with justice and judgment, the habitation of his throne. That is why the world, which cries for justice, will be angry when it comes.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:18
precepts.why:
Everybody says, I can't wait until Jesus comes back. Let's see what the Bible says: “And the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come.” All these nations, countries and religious organizations say they want the Messiah to return, and the Bible prophesies they will be angry.

Why are they angry? Because “Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne.” The Lord is coming with justice and judgment, and the nations don't want that. Many of those nations are living on stolen land, like America. This is stolen land. They are lying when they say they can't wait. Christ's wrath is coming; he's not coming to hand out lollipops and hugs and kisses.

“and the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great.” You know what that reward is? Power. He's going to give his servants power.

“and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth.” That's them. They say the aerosols in the black and brown community are destroying the ozone layer, not their rockets and missiles. All that climate change global BS: they are the ones destroying the earth, digging up and sucking out the oil that is meant to lubricate the tectonic plates, and then they wonder why the earthquakes are happening. They know it, and that's why they will be angry at his return. None calleth for the justice of God.

thread.label: Isaiah 59:5-8
thread.text: They hatch cockatrice’ eggs, and weave the spider’s web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: Matthew 3:7-8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59:5 says “They hatch cockatrice’ eggs”, and a cockatrice is like a poisonous snake. Put together everything from verses two to four, the iniquities that separated us from our God, the hands defiled with blood, the lips that have spoken lies, and this is what comes of it: “he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.” The eggs that are crushed are the kids that come out: a little baby snake. They produce evil followers.

Many years ago at a community meeting a black woman screamed at the police that they were selling drugs in her building and nobody was doing anything. The police set up a sting and locked up two dudes putting drugs in the mailboxes: her own sons. Then she came back saying it was false, with them on video. These are the eggs, the snake eggs coming out.

John the Baptist saw the same thing: “But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers”. That is the same thing Isaiah was talking about. “who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”.

A generation of vipers cannot just say it repents. You have to bring forth God's commandments in application; that is what proves your repentance.

precepts.label: Matthew 12:34
precepts.why:
Now Christ is speaking to them: “O generation of vipers”. That goes back to Isaiah 59, the cockatrice' eggs that break out into a viper. Christ called them vipers, and John the Baptist called them vipers. And their children are little snakes too.

“how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.” What is in the heart comes out of the mouth. A generation of vipers cannot speak good things, because what fills their heart is evil.

That is Isaiah 59 again. Before verse 5, verse 3 said our lips have spoken lies and our tongue perverseness. The lips speak lies and the tongue perverseness because the heart is full of iniquity, and the eggs they hatch are the same kind as the ones who laid them.

precepts.label: Isaiah 65:2
precepts.why:
“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. See what our people do: they walk after their own thoughts. They don't give a damn what the Bible says; I do what I want to do.

And their thoughts are the white man's thoughts. Our people follow all these man-made religions, and they don't teach God's laws, his commandments, his statutes. We ain't got to keep no laws, because that is what all these white people were teaching: don't keep no laws.

So what do you get? Those vipers hatch eggs, and what comes out? Little vipers, little snakes. Your son, little Tyrone, is a snake, and your daughter, little Chenique, was a snake too. That is what God is saying in Isaiah 59:5, and it is why verse 7 says “their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity”: a rebellious people walking after their own thoughts.

precepts.label: Job 8:13-15
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59 says they “weave the spider’s web” and “Their webs shall not become garments”. Job explains the spider's web. “So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish: Whose hope shall be cut off”, because they are hypocrites, “and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.”

Their trust shall be as a spider's web: you get tangled up in that thing, and that spider comes out and bites you and eats you up.

“He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.” Your house won't stand. A people who forget God weave their webs and lean on what they built, but it cannot cover them or hold them up. That is why Isaiah 59:6 goes on, “neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:1-2
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59:6 says “neither shall they cover themselves with their works”, and Isaiah 30 shows the covering they use instead. “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me”: they are looking for counsel, but not from God. “and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit”, not according to the Bible, “that they may add sin to sin”.

“That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth”. At that time it was actual Egypt, but today it's America, spiritual Egypt. They have not asked the prophets what the Bible says. They go “to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!” America ain't the real Egypt, but it is the shadow of Egypt, and our people trust in it.

That is why the act of violence is in their hands. A cruise line banned passengers for life over a brawl in the buffet; graduation ceremonies break out into fights with families arrested, a day of celebration turned into chaos. Our people have made crooked paths for themselves, following the Democratic or the Republican party, the cross and the white Jesus, and whosoever goes therein shall not know peace.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:29
precepts.why:
“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men.” We got eyes, but we act like we ain't got none. We act like what we just saw didn't happen. The curse said it would be so: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

We are like blind people, but we have eyes. We see we're not prospering as a people. We see we're under constant oppression as a people. But we act like we don't see it, because oppression has become so normal to us; it's our everyday life.

It's high noon, but in our minds we are so spiritually blind it is like night for us. “we are in desolate places as dead men”: that's the black and brown community, desolate places, our people like the walking dead. Isaiah 59 is Deuteronomy 28:29 in real time.

That is why verse 9 says, “Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us.” We want to live filthy lives, evil lives, violent lives, and then expect justice from God. It don't work like that. Oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 11:12-13
precepts.why:
There is a difference between being spiritually slow and being spiritually dead. “we are in desolate places as dead men,” but Sirach shows what the nation needs: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” We usually read it as an individual, but think about it on a bigger scale. You might say this is Joe or Bob. No, this is us.

Slow, needing help, lacking ability, full of poverty: that is our people. “yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate,” and lifted up his head from misery, so that many that saw it marvelled at him.

The nations are going to marvel when God raises us up. It will be such a shock that this low, degenerate race of people is now going to rule the earth. We lack the ability now; it is the Lord's eye that sets us up from our low estate.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:20-21
precepts.why:
“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel; think of it as whatever IUIC school you come from. Every camp leader, the head of the sanctuary, must be able to identify the gold brothers and the silver brothers, the gold sisters and silver sisters, and also look through the school and say, this brother and this sister is earth, this one is wood.

If you can't discern that, you'll have problems in the school, putting people in positions that don't fit them. Marcus Garvey had his ships and put his best friends over them, and they didn't know how to run a ship: one crashed, one went to his girlfriend's house, and he lost it all because of friendship. Shake the friendship appointments. Who is best qualified? Who knows what they're doing? A dummy who doesn't study set up as a school leader, and all hell breaks loose. If sanctuary leaders have no discernment, they are spiritually blind and destined for ruin.

Some brothers and sisters are just slow and need more time to grow. Fine; don't put them in that position yet if others are better qualified. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge yourself from the wood and earth spirits. They see this truth not as a government, not as the mustard seed of a government, but as a social club, dancing every new moon and confused when it comes to God's work. That is how a people groping like the blind becomes vessels unto honour.

precepts.label: John 3:18-21
precepts.why:
The voices of our people conceive and utter from the heart words of falsehood, lies on top of lies. Christ answers: “He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.” If you believe on the black Messiah, you are not condemned; if you believe not, you're not even keeping commandment one.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Christ is that light that came into the world, and men love darkness, sin, rather than light, Christ and keeping the commandments. It didn't change from Isaiah to John; it's the same thing: “we wait for light, but behold obscurity.”

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.” They hate Christ, they hate keeping the laws, they hate the commandments, because if you come to Christ your deeds will be reproved: have no other gods before me, bow down to no graven image, remember the Sabbath, honour your father and your mama, thou shalt not kill. They don't want to hear that.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” We want Christ, the word of God, to make our deeds manifest. What am I? Lord, show me.

precepts.label: Amos 5:10
precepts.why:
“Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.” If you depart from evil by repenting, you make yourself a prey to everybody around you; everybody around you hates your guts now. Amos says the same thing: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

That includes some of your own mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers. They hate the one who rebukes and abhor the one who speaks uprightly, because “truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter.”

“and the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.” There was no true judgment in the earth. The one who departs from evil is hated for it, and the Lord sees it.

precepts.label: Matthew 28:19
precepts.why:
“And I will be found of you, saith the Lord: and I will turn away your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations”. Why does it say from all nations? This is for the Israelite who says there is no Israelite in Africa. No matter where you go on the planet, you are going to find some Israelite; that is why he says all nations, “and from all the places whither I have driven you”.

That is why Christ said, “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations”. Teach the Israelites, because we were scattered in all nations. That is the prophecy. And no matter where we are, we are going to be hated.

That is why IUIC travels to all these countries: to bring our people back to who they are and tell them they are the Israelites. That is why we just had one of the biggest worldwide blitzes, because we understand the scripture and we follow it. As John saw, Christ redeemed us to God by his blood out of every kindred, tongue, people and nation, and the Lord will bring us again into the place whence he caused us to be carried away captive.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:22-23
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says the Lord will gather us from all the nations whither he has driven us, and in all those nations we are hated. Christ said so himself: “And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake”. If Christ, the black Messiah himself, said I am going to be hated of all men, why am I surprised when they hate me? That shows the Christians are not reading this Bible. “but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.”

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” We are not going to be able to cover the whole earth. We will not wake up every single Israelite before Christ comes back; that is what he is saying.

But the Lord will “bring you again into the place whence I caused you to be carried away captive”: Israel, Jerusalem, our land. Everything you see here is temporary. It is a movie, and you already know the end: you win. So why are you bugging out? Some of us turn to liquor and alcohol to deal with the hatred and the trauma. You have to expect the hatred. The problem is you are dying to be loved by people who are never going to love you.

Jeremiah says, “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Paul is talking about the same thing: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” That examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said: let us search and try our ways.

This is a lot of times what we as a people do not want to do: examine ourselves. What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

“Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” You have to prove your own self, whether Christ is in you or not. And that is where turning again to the Lord starts. Jeremiah goes on, “We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned”, and that is why we are in this state, the condition we are in now. A people who will not examine themselves will never see why the Lord has covered himself with a cloud, and will never turn again to him.

precepts.label: Romans 13:11
precepts.why:
Paul says: “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.” Salvation is near. It is high time that we wake up from our sleep.

In order to wake up, we must start by examining ourselves, which is what Jeremiah calls for: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

Waking up is not only knowing who we are. It is searching our own ways, seeing that “We have transgressed and have rebelled”, and turning again to the Lord, lifting up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens. The time is short and salvation is nearer than when we first believed, so there is no time left to stay asleep in the condition we are in.

precepts.label: Romans 7:7
precepts.why:
How do we search and try our ways? Paul shows it: “What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.” I would not know what sin is, but by the law. I would not know what lust is, except the law told me.

So by studying the word of God, you are able to self-examine. You are able to search and try your ways, by studying and reading the word of God. That is what Paul said, and it is what Jeremiah said: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.”

Without the law a man has no measure to try himself by; he thinks what he is doing is fine. With the law in front of him, he can see where “We have transgressed and have rebelled”, and why the Lord has not pardoned. The law is the mirror, and the one who reads it is the one who can turn again.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 12:10-11
precepts.why:
The fourth kingdom “shall be strong as iron”. It began with Rome, and America and Europe are the extension of Rome, the iron of the feet. Now Sirach: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” Who is that iron? The fourth kingdom that rules the earth today, Europe and America, the white man.

Who is your enemy? In the 1950s you understood who your enemy was. In the 1800s you understood. Forty or fifty years ago you understood. God says never trust him. As iron rusts, the rust will always appear again, and that is his wickedness. Even though he said, we changed, we gave you civil rights, we are not oppressing you anymore, you see the wickedness coming back now, and they are taking it all back. His kingdom is made of iron, and that wickedness will always return.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him”. He acts like he loves black people and cares about them. Beware of that iron. “and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” If you are righteous and have wisdom, you see all his wickedness as in a looking glass: look at their history. They are a genocidal race of people, and you cannot get justice from them. Look at Palestine, Lebanon and the Congo, hundreds of thousands dead, while the ones running the courts don't stop it. This whole system is unjust.

That is why Daniel says the iron shall “mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”. After 1945 Britain opened itself to the people of its colonies, and after civil rights everybody started coming to America. The white man said he changed, and brought the same people he colonized and destroyed to live among him. Decades later they say they should never have let any of them in. The white man did not change; he is the same person, his rust has not been wiped away, and white people and everybody else are not going to get along.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:6-7
precepts.why:
Hosea says the children of Israel “shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod”. Daniel 12 gives the time frame for it. “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?” The wonders are our people being destroyed, enslaved and colonized, being without a king, without a prince, without an ephod.

“it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is a hundred years; times is two hundred, three hundred in all; and an half makes 350 years. “and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.” Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed. All that power was gone from us; we forgot who we are, and we even forgot our nationality.

When we fled Jerusalem in 70 AD, was our power destroyed? Our country was destroyed, but we went to Africa and built cities there, and the ten tribes were set up on this side of the world doing their thing too. We still had governments, we still had kings over us, and we still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power of the holy people was scattered.

That is the many days without a king: without political sovereignty, when Europe colonized Ghana, Nigeria, Angola, Senegal, Papua New Guinea and the Congo, and when the transatlantic slave trade took us. It is without an image: our minds destroyed until the sisters in Africa bleach their skin and put on weaves, because worshipping the God of your oppressor destroys the way you look at yourself. The same curses fell on our people all over Africa, like the Mau Mau in Kenya, tortured in British camps and paid less than 4,000 pounds each. That is why I don't want no damn reparations.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:11
precepts.why:
Daniel 12 gives the time frame for when our people would be without a king, without an image, and without a sacrifice, as Hosea 3:4 says. Verse 11 reads: “And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.”

The daily sacrifice taken away is Hosea's “without a sacrifice”. Without the sacrifice, the image and the ephod, all our religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance was stripped away, and there was no priest to guide us and tell us what God needs us to do. The white man came in, whipped us, taught us white Jesus and his lies, and forced it down our throats in Africa. After he brought the slaves over here, he went to Africa and destroyed them there, until the people in Africa don't even know that we in the Caribbean and America are the same people.

So from the taking away of the sacrifice, the days are counted, and the question Daniel asked, “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?”, is answered with a set time. That goes back to the yoke of iron upon thy neck until thou have been destroyed: it did not just happen to us over here, it happened to our people in Africa, and the scattering of the holy people runs its appointed course.

There was a promise made to us and our ancestors: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.” A kingdom of priests. That is what Israel was called to be.

Usually we jump over to Malachi 2:7, but the verse tells you right there: the knowledge is the law of God, his laws, his commandments, his statutes. Because we forgot it, he rejected us from that priesthood.

That is why we are destroyed as a race, as a people, mentally and spiritually. The twelve tribes of Israel are a destroyed race. This is why other races come into our communities and run the hospitals, the stores, the clinics. The black man and the brown man do have the ability, and many of us have the knowledge to do it, but they do not want us to have the capabilities.

precepts.label: Luke 1:68-72
precepts.why:
Zephaniah says, “The Lord hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy”. Luke shows how he does it: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. That horn of salvation is Christ, the black Messiah.

“As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. Our people ask, what did we do to you? Why do you hate us so much? You want to know the answer? Christ is coming back to save you from the hand of all that hate you.

Why are you worried that your enemies hate you? Your enemies are not supposed to love you; they were created to hate you. The problem is you think you have no enemies. It is a good thing they hate us, and they should continue: they hate us when we are in our righteousness, not when we are in the streets. So don't worry about those that hate you. Rejoice.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant”. The mercy promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob is that the kingdom is ours. That is why Zephaniah says, “Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart”. Rejoice in the law, rejoice on the Sabbath, rejoice to be among the brothers and sisters. Our judgment is almost ended, and we have a short time here, so why are you bugging out? “The king of Israel, even the Lord, is in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more.”

thread.text: Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.

precepts.label: Psalms 78:68
precepts.why:
“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord”: the north is North America. “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven”: we are scattered everywhere. Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion.” Zion right there refers to Judah.

“But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” See that? Judah is the mount Zion which he loved. So Zechariah is saying, deliver thyself, O Judah, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon, with the so-called Caucasians, here in North America.

Judah has a work to do. Moses blessed him: “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people: let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.” Judah would be the one going out to teach, to find the tribes and teach them the word of God. Not only would Judah be fighting in the system he lives in; a remnant of them would wake up, go out, teach and gather the twelve tribes of Israel. Help Judah against his enemies, against the white man.

And Jacob said: “Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies”: always struggling, always fighting, and not for no reason, but for the liberation of his people. “thy father’s children shall bow down before thee”, because Judah would be in the forefront teaching and gathering the tribes. “Judah is a lion’s whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?” What happened? They gave us crack, heroin, feminism, bad education, all that the white man did to us, and Judah just rolled over and went to sleep. Now we just want money; the fight is gone. But the true liberation comes from the teachers of the Bible.

precepts.label: Psalms 137:7-8
precepts.why:
Zion dwells with the daughter of Babylon. Who is the daughter of Babylon? “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof. O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed.” The children of Edom, E-D-O-M, meaning red people. So Edom is called the daughter of Babylon, and Judah dwells with Edom here in North America.

How do we deliver ourselves? “And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” That's how we deliver ourselves: by not being partakers in the sins of America, not taking part in their religious ceremonies, their denominations, their political groups and traditions. It's the same thing 2 Corinthians 6:17 says. “For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities. Reward her even as she rewarded you, and double unto her double according to her works.” Who is the you? The tribes of Israel. America is going to get double what they did to us, just as the psalm says: “happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.”

It may look like we've been forsaken, but “Israel hath not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, of the Lord of hosts; though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.” We are in a low state, destitute, degenerate as a people: the twerkers, the drug dealers, the homeless ones, that's how it's put out there. Regardless of all that, God has not forsaken us. “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel.” There is still hope for the pimps and the hoes, the prostitutes, the baby mama drama and the baby daddies.

“Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul: be not cut off in her iniquity; for this is the time of the Lord’s vengeance; he will render unto her a recompence.” The way you flee is to deliver your soul, and the way you deliver your soul is through repentance and keeping God's commandments.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:18
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “The Lord of hosts shall defend them”, and “the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.” He is not saving all nations; he is only saving the twelve tribes. Christ says the same of his people: “And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

This rock is Christ himself. “I will build my church”: the church is the twelve tribes of Israel. And “the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

So although Britain forbade us to march, trying to hinder black excellence, hinder black unity, hinder the twelve tribes of Israel growing, Christ said the gates of hell will not prevail. They delayed the men's conference, but it still went on, and the presentations were still done. Bishops, deacons, captains, officers of thousands and officers of hundreds all know what the leadership knows, so if one is taken up there are thousands of other men who know exactly the same thing. This will not be stopped.

That is how the Lord defends them. He bends Judah as his bow, fills the bow with Ephraim, and raises up the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece, Esau, Edom, the so-called white man, making us as the sword of a mighty man. His arrow goes forth as the lightning, he goes with the whirlwinds of the south, the chariots of God, and we devour and subdue with sling stones. The church he builds on the rock cannot be stopped.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 11:28
precepts.why:
Zechariah ends with the Lord saving “the flock of his people”, lifted up “as the stones of a crown”, filled like the bowls and the corners of the altar, drinking and making “a noise as through wine”. At the breaking of bread the class read Paul's instruction for those who drink of the Lord's cup now: “But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup.”

It is the same instruction the class opened with in Lamentations: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Before a man eats of that bread and drinks of that cup, he has to search himself and try his ways.

So the cup of the Lord now is a call to examine ourselves and turn again to the Lord. The wine and the rejoicing of Zechariah belong to the flock he saves in that day: the twelve tribes that searched and tried their ways and turned back to him, the stones of his crown lifted up upon his land.

Some of our kids lie right in your face, insulting your intelligence, acting like they don't know what you are really asking, as if the Lord isn't hearing it. All of this is purged before we get to the kingdom. None of that evil is going to make it there.

precepts.label: Luke 19:27

Zechariah says that when any shall yet prophesy lies, “his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live”, and “shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.” Why would his own father and mother do that? Because they will have already witnessed how Christ dealt with the rebellious. Christ said it: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.”

Everybody that is against what Christ said is an enemy of Christ, and that includes our people. You fathers and mothers try to rule over your children to keep them from going astray, and they say, I'm not having that; I'm doing my own thing; the hell with what you got to say, mama; the hell with that Bible. They refuse the correction of their fathers and mothers ruling over them, and they would not that Christ and his law should reign over them.

This happens in the wilderness. Christ will be teaching the commandments face to face, and some will still tell him, I ain't doing this, I ain't doing that. Christ said, bring them here, and kill them right in front of my feet.

Once those parents see that Christ ain't playing, that is how they will be moving: you want to put my head on the chopping block? You will die right now. So to you brothers and sisters with sons and daughters that refuse to change: don't put your life on the line for wickedness that refuses to repent. We pray our brothers and sisters get their minds right now, so they don't end up there.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:26
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness.” What is the fountain? The fountain opened to the nation of Israel is the Bible, the laws of the Most High.

In that day the laws of God will be opened up to the twelve tribes of Israel, with Christ there. It is for sin and for uncleanness: the lies, the wickedness and the evil will be opened up to be judged.

That day is in the wilderness, right before we get to our kingdom. It parallels Ezekiel, where the Lord pleads with us face to face and says, I will cause you to pass under the rod: the rod of correction. Christ will cause all of us, sons and daughters, mothers and fathers, to pass under that rod, washed by the word. If we have not learned to keep God's laws by then, that is the day of judgment.

That is why the names of the idols are cut off and no more remembered. When the Lord smites down the one teaching lies, everybody instantly drops what he taught; nobody talks about it anymore. The fountain of the word cleanses the nation, and everything that is not in line with this Bible is put to death with the ones that taught it.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 7:27-28
precepts.why:
“For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother”. This is not a commandment man stated; God commanded it. Honour means moral integrity, honesty and a strong code of conduct, a high respect, toward your father and your mother. “And, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death”: that is the judgment for not honouring them.

Sirach gives the measure of it: “Honour thy father with thy whole heart”. The root word for integrity is integer, meaning whole. Honour them with your whole heart. “And forget not the sorrows of thy mother”: the troubles she went through, carrying you for nine months and giving birth to you.

“Remember that thou wast begotten of them”. You came from them. “And how canst thou recompense them the things that they have done for thee?” How can you pay them back for bringing you into this world? You cannot. They did it because it was their responsibility.

So your responsibility as the child is to honour that alone: for nothing else but the fact that they brought you into this world and raised you. That is why our daughters are warned: the ones who walk away from their parents' protection for a boyfriend's sweet nothings can end up like the young woman sentenced to fifteen years, never to see that boyfriend again.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 3:10-13
precepts.why:
“Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father’s dishonour is no glory unto thee.” Some who are older have parents who are not in this truth, and they might think that because their parent is not in the truth they do not have to give them the respect of a parent. That is not what the Lord said. It is no glory that your father or mother is not in this truth, and nothing to glory in because the Lord called you.

“For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father; and a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.”

“My son, help thy father in his age, and grieve him not as long as he liveth.” You are to be an aid to your parent when they reach a certain age, and not just when you feel like it. “And if his understanding fail, have patience with him”. We are the only nation of people that does not take care of our elders. Where do you think nursing homes come from? The children do not want to deal with their parents at a certain age, so they pay somebody else to watch after them. That is how we honour our parents.

The Deacon has a real disdain for children who do not honour their parents, because his died when he was young and he went through the system with no mother and father, though his grandparents took him in. To have your parents, and be able to have a conversation with them, and still not respect that: that is a problem.

“And despise him not when thou art in thy full strength.” Be patient, because the example we set is what the young men see; we are their goalpost.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 4:15-16
precepts.why:
“For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil.” The rulers are a terror to those that do evil. Peter shows the difference between the two kinds of suffering: “But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.” One of the titles for this class was going to be suffer not as a murderer.

“Yet if any man suffer as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.” Suffering as a Christian means suffering as one that follows Christ and the commandments of God, not Christianity. If we get locked up for doing what is right, and some of us will, we suffer that and glorify God.

The young man in the courtroom is suffering as a murderer, literally. He cannot say the Lord is going to repay them for what they are doing to him; the reason he is being judged is that he broke the laws of the Most High. He broke down crying because he is a wankster, not a gangster. Where are the homies and the shoot-em-up videos now? When you get locked up, nobody cares about your black ass once you are in jail. Esau is the devil for a reason; he lets the little negro run around with a gun killing his own people, and then he busts him, and he becomes property of the state, sweat equity for the prison system.

That is where many of our sons and daughters are going when they refuse to listen to their parents: if not jail, a pregnancy, a disease, a marriage riddled with alcohol abuse and domestic violence. That is why God gave children parents. We were not afraid of the power before; we broke the commandments, so the Lord put this beast over us, and when you mess up with him he has no pity. As they say in the islands, those who don’t hear will feel. Suffer, if you must, as a follower of Christ, never as an evildoer.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:10
precepts.why:
“For rulers are not a terror to good works”. The powers that be are not a terror to those of us that keep the commandments of God. Even though we are persecuted for it, it is not a terror to us, because we know what it is about. We are in captivity, but we are doing what God said to do, and they are going to have to answer to the Father for their mistreatment of us.

That is because of this promise: “Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” If I am going to get locked up for doing what is right, I will suffer for that.

All the words they say to me will not mean anything, because I am suffering for a worthy cause, and I know that after that, mine is the kingdom of heaven. You can go through that trial and say, the Lord is going to receive me because I did what was right.

That is a totally different mentality than going in as a murderer. Suffering as a murderer, you are still going to get jacked up at the end; you are not getting the kingdom. So do that which is good, and if the rulers persecute you for it, the kingdom of heaven is yours.
