precepts.label: Deuteronomy 6:25
precepts.why:
“Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” To know who the unrighteous are, you have to know what righteousness is, and the law defines it: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

That is what righteousness is: observing to do all the commandments before the Lord, as he commanded. So the unrighteous who will not inherit the kingdom are those who will not do the commandments.

That is the problem with Christianity. It is not that the Lord's arm is too short or his ear too heavy; it is that your sins have separated between you and your God. They are not trying to transform their lives to that of the nation of Israel according to the holy scriptures. And that is why Paul lists fornicators, idolaters, adulterers and the rest: every one of them breaks the commandments that are our righteousness.

precepts.label: Romans 10:1-4
precepts.why:
The Christian says, oh no, that's not the righteousness; go to Romans 10:4: “For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.” See, we ain't got to keep no laws, so that cancels out Deuteronomy 6:25. No, numbskull. We don't run from scriptures; we explain and edify on the scriptures.

Christ is the end of the law of animal sacrifice for righteousness. Christ took the place of the animal sacrifice. And where they think they have you, “to every one that believeth”, read verse one for the context: “Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.”

The whole subject is Israel being saved. Israel had “a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge”, “going about to establish their own righteousness”. Christ is our righteousness in the law because he suffered and took the place of the law of sacrifice. That does not do away with the commandments of Deuteronomy 6:25; it is why the unrighteous, who will not keep them, still shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:28
precepts.why:
“Be not deceived: neither fornicators”, “nor adulterers”. Fornication covers the whole list of sexual sins in Leviticus 18. And for the porno brothers, Christ said: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.”

So porn falls into that category. It is adultery in the heart, and adulterers shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

Who still struggles with porn? Not who is always watching; who still struggles with it? Nine hands went up in the room. The fight is real, and it has to be named for what it is before it can be fought.

precepts.label: Romans 6:12-15
precepts.why:
“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” The word reign means to rule: don't let sin rule your mortal body. Every brother says, I got the porn under control, I am in control. There's no such thing as control of sin. Once you start obeying that lust, it has you in control; you don't have it in control.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.” Men and women are alive from the dead. We have to submit ourselves to Christ; he is our commander, our leader, and what he says we must do.

“For sin shall not have dominion over you”: Paul is reiterating. Dominion goes back to reign in verse 12. “for ye are not under the law”, the law of sacrifice, “but under grace”, the grace of Christ. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace?” Should we keep watching porn because we're not under the law of sacrifice? “God forbid.”

One brother said, I got it under control. In a store, thinking about porn, he was on his phone looking at it, forgot where he was, took his pecker out and started looking at all the ladies. Does that sound like he had it under control? He got arrested; he's in jail. Another decided to look at porn while he drove home, and bam, he crashed. It has you in check. You need a checklist in your mind so you can say, I'm messed up, I need help, because I could die or I could be in jail. That is sin reigning, and the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:76-78
precepts.why:
What happens when sin reigns in your body and has dominion over you? “And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” He is the guide of those who keep his commandments and precepts.

“let not your sins weigh you down”: sometimes you fall in the midst of sin, and Satan gets in your ear and whispers, you're no good, you need to leave this truth, the Lord can't use a person like you. Well, he used Samson. He used David. He used a lot of our forefathers that fell to sin. “and let not your iniquities lift up themselves”: don't let them rise back up in your body again.

“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through!” You may say, I'm not bound with my sin. Bound in your sins is sin reigning in your body and having dominion over you. Just like no man can travel through that path, we can't reach you with the scriptures any more. Your heart is hardened, your sin has dominated your life, and you're not you anymore. The scriptures have no effect on you.

“It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Death and destruction: that is the final outcome, brothers. Stop watching the porn. “And such were some of you: but ye are washed”: that is the way out, not staying bound.

precepts.label: Luke 21:15
precepts.why:
“For the mystery of iniquity doth already work”: that is Rome, already working in the apostles’ time, “until he be taken out of the way.” “And then shall that Wicked be revealed.” Why does the wicked need to be revealed? Because he does not present himself as the wicked. He has transformed into an angel of light, into Lucifer, and people think he is the righteous. But God’s witnesses, the Israelites, the prophets that are waking up, will testify who the wicked is and reveal him: the so-called white man, the nation of Edom, the people God hates. For years we have said it and many did not believe; now he is showing you who he is.

Then: “whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming.” Two things: consuming him with the spirit of his mouth, and destroying him with the brightness of his coming. What is the spirit of his mouth?

“For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.” That mouth and wisdom is Christ speaking through us, the Holy Spirit dwelling in us, so that nobody can gainsay us. That is the kind of power the Lord has given us.

So as we teach the word of God, the wicked are being consumed with the spirit of the Lord’s mouth, because we are bringing forth judgment. The Lord speaks through His witnesses, and their testimony condemns the wicked before his destruction at the brightness of Christ’s coming.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:18
precepts.why:
“And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.” We are going to be brought before governors and kings as a testimony against them. The testimony is us teaching the Bible, the laws and the testimonies, letting them know: God is coming back to destroy you. You are wicked. You have been stealing land, you have been murdering, you are the wicked of the earth.

When you testify on this earth, you are condemning people. Everybody who hears the word of God and turns their back on it is condemned. Every white person hearing about the Israelites and hearing these teachings, many of them online, is hearing that the Lord is going to judge Edom and judge Amalek, and those who call themselves Jews and are not. We are bringing forth judgment on the earth.

“But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak. For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.” Do not worry what to say before kings. It will not be you speaking; the spirit that dwells in us takes over, and it is the Lord judging them with your voice.

That is how the Lord consumes the wicked “with the spirit of his mouth.” 2 Esdras 11 shows it too: the roaring lion that sends out a man’s voice unto the eagle, which is Rome, with Europe and America as its extension. That voice is the prophets, the witnesses on the earth today, condemning Edom for all the evil he has done through the centuries.

precepts.label: Zechariah 4:11
precepts.why:
“What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the candlestick and upon the left side thereof?” Zechariah asks again about “these two olive branches which through the two golden pipes empty the golden oil out of themselves.” The oil is understanding. The answer: “These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.”

The two anointed ones are the two witnesses. In Zechariah’s time they were Joshua the priest and Zerubbabel. Before Babylon it was Isaiah and Jeremiah; in Revelation 11 it is Moses and Elijah. Different names, different people, but the same pattern: God always sends his prophets forth in twos before he brings forth judgment.

That is why Christ sent the twelve and the seventy elders out two by two. You cannot make judgment without two witnesses. And when the witnesses come they bind and loose things on earth, they forgive and they condemn, because it is the Lord speaking through them.

The two witnesses also speak of Israel as a whole. God says his people are his witnesses; and there are the two sticks, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, the northern and southern kingdom. A witness has a testimony, and Israel is sent to testify on this earth before the judgment comes.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:18
precepts.why:
“For thy help will I send my servants”: God says he is going to send Isaiah and Jeremiah. And that is what happened. Isaiah and Jeremiah came and prophesied before Babylon came and destroyed Jerusalem.

That is the pattern behind “I will give power unto my two witnesses.” God always sends forth witnesses before he brings forth judgment, and he sends them in twos. Isaiah and Jeremiah before Babylon; Joshua and Zerubbabel in Zechariah’s day; Moses and Elijah in Revelation 11. Christ sent the apostles and the seventy out in twos for the same reason: you need two witnesses to bring forth judgment.

So the two witnesses of Revelation 11 are the two major prophets that come before the end, and they also speak of Israel as a whole, the people God calls his witnesses on this earth. Judgment does not fall until the witnesses have prophesied.

As we teach the word of God, we are marking them for destruction, and every last one of our enemies is going to be destroyed with fire when Christ returns. “If any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed”: that is how they are going to die when Christ returns.

That is why Esau will try to kill the witnesses. He does not want judgment to come on him, and when the witnesses testify, judgment comes. As we teach his word, they are going to try to kill us, because they do not want us to testify.

The witnesses also “have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy”, to turn the waters to blood, “and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will.” As often as they prophesy, the earth is smitten with plagues.

After we finish testifying the laws and the testimonies, everything the prophets say, revealing who Edom is and who the synagogue of Satan is, judging everybody on the earth, they are going to kill us because of our testimony.

Revelation 12:17 says the same: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” The dragon is Edom. He makes war with those of us that keep the commandments and are teaching the word of God, the laws and the testimonies.

Revelation 18 shows where: “Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her.” The apostles and prophets are here in America today, all twelve of them, teaching; and after they finish their testimony they will be killed. precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:47-48
precepts.why:

Verse 6 says the same: “the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there”. She is nourished “for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.” Who is feeding us from the face of the serpent? The white man is the devil the Bible speaks of. Deuteronomy 28 shows crystal clear who this demon is that's feeding us.

First, why: “Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. It lines up with Luke: these be the days of vengeance, because we broke the commandments of the Lord. We ain't happy to keep the Most High's high holy days. We show joyfulness and gladness of heart for the Fourth of July and these pagan, evil, wicked holidays; but when it comes to Passover, the Sabbath, the day of atonement, the feast of unleavened bread, the beautiful holy days the Lord gave you, you got your lips stuck out. You mad.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. God did that. That is how we're fed: for food, for water, for clothing, even the textiles they stole, for hospital care, for anything you need, you have to go to the same enemy. We don't own nothing. God set it up that way because we made our father mad.

“and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Who put the yoke of iron on our neck? The so-called white man, the serpent of Revelation. The same serpent put a chain around your neck, until you are dead bodies in the street of America, not even knowing who you are, your mind destroyed, celebrating the Fourth of July when your people were in slavery on that same date.

And the evil preachers who deceived us will pay too. Jeremiah 23: woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture. Taking his Bible and lying to God's people with it is a serious crime. So the woman nourished from the face of the serpent is Israel in this captivity, fed by the enemy the Lord sent against us for not serving him with gladness.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:11
precepts.why:
Ezra sees “a roaring lion chased out of the wood”, and he “sent out a man's voice unto the eagle”. The eagle is Rome, and Europe and America are the extension of it. The roaring lion is Christ, but first it is us, the prophets: a man's voice speaking to the eagle. That is the witnesses on the earth today condemning the so-called white man, Edom, for all the evil he has done through the centuries. God has not forgotten slavery, Jim Crow, the destruction of Jerusalem by Rome. He does not forget anything.

How will we overcome that beast? “And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.” We overcome the beast, Edom, by the blood of Christ, and by the word of our testimony.

What is our testimony? The words of the prophets. We are teaching the laws and the words of the prophets, revealing that he has ruled with deceit, set himself up as the Jews and the people of God, and dwelt on this earth “with much wicked oppression”. In a court of law the witnesses must bring their testimony before judgment comes, and the whole earth is our courtroom. When we speak, the Lord is speaking through us, the spirit of his mouth.

And by the blood of the Lamb, meaning Christ having mercy on us. If you make a mistake, fix it. If you are struggling with things inside, fix it. If you fall, get back up; Christ will have mercy on you. But you also have to have his testimony. That is how we overcome this wicked society, and then the eagle, its horrible wings, wicked feathers, malicious heads and hurtful claws, will appear no more.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 12:32
precepts.why:
“For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.” The tribes that left the heathen went into the Euphrates “by the narrow places of the river” and down into the ocean, and the Most High was with them. He showed them signs, and there were men among them able to read those signs.

“And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do; the heads of them were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their commandment.” Issachar could read the stars. That is how they were the navigators: they had understanding of the times, they knew what Israel ought to do, and so they were able to lead the ships as the tribes came over. They knew how to navigate the waters.

They understood the winds and the currents, the Atlantic drift routes from Africa to America. Solomon understood all of this too, with the navy he had going out; the same ports Solomon’s navy knew were the stops along the route, because “through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. African boatmen from Lake Chad later built a papyrus boat on the pattern of the ancient Egyptians and sailed it from North Africa as far as Barbados, proving such a drift journey on the Africa-to-America currents could be done, because the currents were understood.

So the ten tribes did not wander blindly into “a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The Most High showed signs, Issachar read them, and the ships came across into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America. “Then dwelt they there until the latter time”, and that is why we are here in the latter times.

precepts.label: Ezra 1:3-4
precepts.why:
Between verse 40 and verse 41 of 2 Esdras 13 there is a whole lot of history. Verse 40 is Assyria: “whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”, before Babylon and before the Persians. Then Babylon took down Assyria and took her captives, and moved down and took Judah. Then the Persians came in. None of that is mentioned in the two verses; it jumps from Assyria to Persia, under Cyrus. So when verse 41 says “But they took this counsel among themselves”, what is the counsel? Ezra shows it.

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem.” It is Cyrus speaking: the proclamation between the Most High and him, allowing Israel to go back and build in exchange for being able to take down Babylon.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.” That was what was charged to Israel to go and do.

But the counsel the tribes took among themselves was different: “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The bulk of them said, we are not staying; we are not going back to build in Jerusalem; we are going to a further country. Ezra and Nehemiah are the first two books of Ezra, and 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras are the third and fourth, and together they detail this history.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 9:26-28
precepts.why:
“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. If it took us a year and a half to get from one area to another, don’t you think we were making stops? Maritime means things connected with the sea, oceans and navigation: shipping, commerce, naval operations. We were running those ports, and even where it was not us particularly, we had understanding with the nations we passed by. The Red Sea and the Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, with trade to Arabia, India, Persia and China.

Solomon had a navy of ships: “And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion–geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.” Shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: those are the maritime men.

Ezion-geber is at the northern tip of the Red Sea’s Gulf of Aqaba, by modern-day Aqaba in Jordan and Eilat. That is very near the region where the brothers entered into the Euphrates. “And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.” Ophir is not far from those same areas.

So we had maritime trade going on even in Solomon’s time. It was no mystery for us to make it from where we were, out of Persia, over to the Americas, because those ports were there. That is how the journey took a year and a half, stopping at the ports, until we came into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:12
precepts.why:
Solomon’s ships “came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold”. Isaiah uses that same gold: “I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.”

We often read this and keep going, and some will say it is the best gold, but we don’t go deeper into what the gold of Ophir is. The gold of Ophir is an exceptionally fine, pure gold, prized in the ancient world, famous as what King Solomon and King Hiram of Tyre brought in, and its exact location remains one of history’s greatest archaeological mysteries.

That is what the Most High is going to make you men: that pure fine gold. The same tribes who crossed the waters on those old maritime routes, whose record the historians call mythical, are the men the Most High will make more precious than the golden wedge of Ophir.
